correctness.rationale: All positive periods are handled: y has no four-alternating or six-constant factors; for period p coprime to 3 the 5p+1 factor would be constant, and for p divisible by 3 the surjective monotone desubstitution F produces a shorter positive period. In x a divisible-by-3 period descends to a forbidden y period, and a coprime period forces a forbidden alternating block. x[18:33]=(101)^5 proves sharpness. The digit-parity recurrence, quantifiers, boundary endpoints and surjectivity are explicitly reconstructed in RESULT.md; checker independently confirms finite identity and witness.

originality.rationale: Dekking (arXiv:2301.13563v1, Jan 31 2023) states this exact exponent-five assertion as Shallit Conjecture 9; the later published version labels it Conjecture 10. Full-text comparison with arXiv:2602.21895v1 establishes that subsequent uniform-recurrence, symmetry, factor-complexity, and frequency results do not entail the forbidden 5p+1-period factor theorem. OEIS A357448 has the recurrence but no established critical exponent. Targeted published-finding corpus claim/alias and web searches identified no equivalent solution, without establishing uniqueness of discovery.
residual_risks: Search/index coverage does not establish theorem uniqueness or rule out an unindexed independent proof.
The finite checker is not independent peer assessment and is not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Exact solution of a specifically published mathematical conjecture on a canonical arithmetic word. The first bound on arbitrarily long fractional powers and a sharp attaining word give a natural invariant and reusable period-descent structure. Unlike a narrow arbitrary finite parameter slice, the result quantifies every factor at every starting position and positive period.
